original_test_intent: Verify the complete eight-byte SMBIOS Type 4 Processor ID payload for every expected processor record matches the platform-approved architecture-specific signature/feature representation and remains stable after reboot; the field is not assumed to be a unique serial identifier.
original_method: Capture all Type 4 records and raw bytes, bind each to socket/population status, retain Processor ID byte order exactly, interpret signature and feature portions only under the approved CPU architecture/SMBIOS rules, apply any explicit mask, compare with trusted CPU evidence, reboot and repeat.
manual_activity: A user approves CPU-architecture semantics, expected bytes/masks and reboot plan. Raw extraction, masked comparison and persistence checking are automatable.
required_inputs: Approved Processor ID field semantics for the CPU architecture and SMBIOS version
Expected eight-byte payload or signature/feature mask per populated socket
Validated raw/decoded tooling and reboot/OOB plan
safety_requirements: Read SMBIOS/CPU identity only; do not alter processor state or firmware.
Preserve complete Type 4 records, exact byte order and errors; do not compare truncated grep context.
Do not call Processor ID a unique serial, and do not apply x86 CPUID layout to another architecture without authoritative mapping.
Mask only project-approved variable/reserved bits and retain both raw and masked comparison evidence.
Stop on missing/duplicate records, architecture ambiguity, unexplained byte drift or reboot failure; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Collect raw/decoded Type 4 and architecture-appropriate CPU evidence, bind each socket, compare the full bytes using approved semantics/masks and repeat after reboot.
Do not expose data beyond policy, invent masks, modify CPU state or decide PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve architecture/byte semantics, expected bytes or masks, socket mapping and evidence sensitivity.
Resolve firmware versus CPU-reported signature/feature differences and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The label is relevant, but grep may detach ID bytes from socket records, hides errors and does not define byte order, architecture, full-width completeness or masks.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Archive complete decoded and raw Type 4 data with tool/errors, bind Processor ID to socket/status and compare exact eight-byte payloads under the approved architecture-specific rule.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Processor ID scope, Type 4 script and 10/10-minute values are retained.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Retain raw bytes and display order per Type 4 record, decode signature/features only for the approved architecture, cross-check against an independent CPU source where defined, and apply explicit masks without losing raw evidence across reboot.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: SMBIOS Type 4 systems; decoding is CPU-architecture-specific.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record SMBIOS, parser/dmidecode, BIOS, CPU and OS identity-tool revisions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Applicable SMBIOS Type 4 Processor ID architecture rules plus approved processor-vendor identity documentation and installed tooling documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds full-width raw bytes, byte-order/architecture semantics, controlled masking and rejects unique-ID assumptions.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; adds truncation, mapping and decode validation.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: The field commonly represents signature/features rather than a stable per-unit unique identifier; some feature reporting can be firmware-dependent.

project_override_considerations: A project may mask named variable/reserved feature bits or use a signature-only acceptance rule, but must preserve raw eight-byte evidence, list every mask and apply it per mapped socket.
expected_evidence: Approval, architecture semantics, expected payload/mask/socket map and tool/SMBIOS versions
Complete pre-reboot Type 4 table with raw bytes, decoded components and masked comparison
Engineer verdict without unsupported uniqueness claims

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The item clearly targets the Type 4 Processor ID payload; architecture-specific meaning and mask policy are required inputs, not competing source intent.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The payload is safely collectable and the validation operation is identifiable; architecture rules and expected bytes affect readiness.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Replaces line fragments with complete per-socket raw-byte evidence and architecture semantics.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains controlled per-processor mapping while correcting the unique-identity implication and capability to FULLY AUTOMATABLE.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Adds exact width/byte order, architecture-specific decode and auditable mask governance.

review_improvement: Prevents truncated, byte-swapped or wrong-architecture interpretations and avoids treating a signature/feature field as a privacy-sensitive unique CPU serial without evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: After the project supplies architecture-specific semantics and any masks, all collection and comparison steps are software-controlled; missing baseline data do not make the case partial or blocked.
